context_description: A lounge where the chairs are lined up in a row against the walls facing a television, with no grouped seating and a single window high on one wall.

expected_patterns.name: Sitting Circle
expected_patterns.rationale: Chairs ranged along the walls give no natural grouping; a sitting circle is the pattern that turns a row of seats into a place where people face one another and talk.

expected_patterns.name: Different Chairs
expected_patterns.rationale: A uniform row of identical chairs ignores that people are different sizes and want different postures; the pattern calls for a variety of chairs.

expected_patterns.name: Sequence of Sitting Spaces
expected_patterns.rationale: A single undifferentiated lounge offers no gradient from public to intimate seating; the pattern asks for a sequence of distinct sitting places.

expected_patterns.name: Window Place
expected_patterns.rationale: With only a high single window and seats turned to a screen, the room lacks a place to sit in the light by the window.

notes: Space-type case. All four expected patterns are attached to this entity in the extracted corpus and should be returned by `bsos query --type pattern --include-proposed`.

context_description: A deep-plan two-storey detached house: rooms strung off a central corridor, most rooms lit from one side only, and a flat roof with no sheltering overhang.

expected_patterns.name: Wings of Light
expected_patterns.rationale: A deep plan forces single-aspect rooms; wings of light keeps every room narrow enough to be daylit from two sides.

expected_patterns.name: The Flow Through Rooms
expected_patterns.rationale: Rooms hung off a dead corridor break the movement of the house; the pattern restores a looping flow from room to room.

expected_patterns.name: Sheltering Roof
expected_patterns.rationale: A flat roof with no overhang denies the house its sheltering form; the pattern wants a roof that comes down low around the building.

notes: Space-type case (a dwelling configuration). All three expected patterns are attached to this entity in the extracted corpus.

context_description: A single bench bolted to a blank corridor wall, facing the opposite wall, with nothing to look at and no other seats nearby.

expected_patterns.name: Sequence of Sitting Spaces
expected_patterns.rationale: An isolated bench is not part of any graded sequence of places to rest; the pattern places seats along a journey rather than singly.

expected_patterns.name: Windows Overlooking Life
expected_patterns.rationale: A bench facing a blank wall has nothing worth watching; seating should be placed where it overlooks activity. Domain judgement; may be absent from the extracted corpus and reported as missing.

notes: Component-type case. 'Sequence of Sitting Spaces' is attached to this entity in the corpus; 'Windows Overlooking Life' is a reviewer expectation that may be reported missing — that gap is the regression signal.

context_description: An enclosed dog-leg fire stair tucked into a corner, dark and purely utilitarian, with no daylight and no relation to the life of the building.

expected_patterns.name: Staircase as a Stage
expected_patterns.rationale: A hidden utilitarian stair misses the chance for the staircase to be a social place; the pattern makes the stair a stage onto the room it serves.

expected_patterns.name: Light on Two Sides of Every Room
expected_patterns.rationale: A dark enclosed stair shaft is unpleasant and feels unsafe; daylight from more than one direction makes it usable. Domain judgement; may be absent and reported as missing.

notes: System-type case. 'Staircase as a Stage' is attached in the corpus; the lighting expectation may be reported missing.
